rules.statement: The coding hub distinguishes guest and signed-in access, independently settling domain mastery, resume work and ranking.
Coding submissions require authentication and return both submission and asynchronous job identities.
Mock interview session selection is performed on the server from course, level and kind and the session is persisted.
Playground selection opens a distinct setup surface before the live session.
Entering a Playground requires every declared readiness check and remains an explicit learner action.
Reloading setup resumes an available open session before creating a replacement session.
A live-session deep link without a prior successful machine pair returns the learner to setup.
A connection drop after a successful pair keeps the learner in the live session and exposes reconnect guidance.
The live workspace anatomy follows the Playground kind while preserving one shared guided-session shell.
Mock interview setup never presents generic journey progress; progress is shown only after session creation when a server-confirmed current phase or turn and total are both available.
A learner has at most one resumable mock interview session per course, and that session is the primary action on return.
Starting a new mock interview while one is resumable requires explicit abandonment confirmation; replacement never silently discards confirmed work.
Interview format and target level are the only required setup choices and become immutable after session creation; the course is inherited from Learn.
Submitted turns and the server-confirmed session position are recovery authority across refresh, reconnect and leaving Learn.
Interview mode does not expose scores or coaching between turns unless a separately declared coaching format is selected.
A completed interview passes through explicit submitting and grading states; delayed or failed grading never appears as a completed result.
Assessment claims are traceable to submitted answers and the declared rubric, and recommendations remain inside the current course context.
Only graded attempts enter history and only sufficiently comparable graded attempts produce a progress trend; otherwise the learner sees an insufficient-data explanation.
Every empty, delayed and failed mock interview state exposes a truthful recovery action.

acceptance.statement: Practice, coding problem, playground and mock interview route families mount their declared surfaces.
Submitting code returns submission and job identities for asynchronous judging.
Starting a mock interview server-draws and persists a session for the chosen course, level and kind.
A first-time learner can understand the interview format, expected effort and assessment output before starting, without a decorative setup progress indicator.
The Playground journey exposes catalog, explicit readiness setup and a guarded live session as distinct surfaces with reconnect behavior.
A learner with an unfinished interview sees Resume as the primary action with the last server-confirmed position, and starting new requires explicit abandonment.
The active interview shows progress only from a real server-confirmed current phase or turn and format total.
Refresh, reconnect and leaving Learn preserve every submitted turn and the last confirmed interview position.
Completing the format passes through explicit submitting and grading states before any assessed result is shown.
Delayed or failed assessment exposes retry or return-later recovery and never appears as a completed result.
The result connects rubric context, submitted-answer evidence, strengths, gaps, course content and a next practice action.
History and progress distinguish no data, insufficient comparable data and a supported trend.
Concurrent or stale session advancement cannot silently overwrite the server-confirmed interview position.

unknowns.question: Which playground session state is durable across devices?
unknowns.impact: The routed surfaces prove setup and session entry, but the cited backend operations in this feature do not establish cross-device persistence semantics.

unknowns.question: What phase or turn totals, expected durations and rubric versions belong to each interview format and target level?
unknowns.impact: The business journey requires a declared format contract but does not invent exact values; architecture and backend contract work must assign their authority.

unknowns.question: What minimum sample and comparability dimensions permit an interview progress trend?
unknowns.impact: Progress must remain in an insufficient-data state until the approved analytics rule defines a trustworthy comparison.

evidence.claim: The coding hub exposes guest/signed-in access, domain mastery, resume work and ranked standing.

The playground session route mounts the live session page.
The mock interview route mounts the setup page.

The interview result route mounts the result page.
